extracted.intended_audience: LaTeX users and package authors using the pgf/TikZ graphics system (people implementing or using point/path/snakes commands)
extracted.subtask_short: tikz pgf path and point commands
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for pgf/TikZ commands that construct and manipulate points and paths (point-returning primitives, path construction ops, bounding-box internals, and the 'snakes' subsystem). Includes command semantics, options, examples, and warnings.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfpointlineattime
rubrics_metrics.description: Yields a point that is the tth fraction between p and q, i.e., p + t(q − p). For t = 1/2 this is the middle of p and q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use t between 0 and 1 to interpolate; example diagram labels intermediate fractions (0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfpointlineatdistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Yields a point that is located <distance> many units removed from the start point in the direction of the end point (travel <distance> steps from start toward end).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distance is in TeX dimensions (e.g., pt). Examples show points at 0pt, 20pt, 40pt, 70pt along a segment.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfpointcurveattime
rubrics_metrics.description: Yields a point that is on the Bézier curve from p to q with the support points s1 and s2. The time t determines the location; t = 0 yields p and t = 1 yields q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use t values in [0,1]; examples show points at t=0,0.25,0.5,0.75,1. Consult a standard computer-graphics text for Bézier background.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfpointborderrectangle
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the point at the intersection of the ray starting at the origin towards (direction point) and a rectangle centered at the origin with upper-right corner at (corner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The direction point should have length 'about 1pt' but will be normalized automatically; using a length near 1pt reduces rounding errors. Used by shape mechanism to compute border points.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfpointborderellipse
rubrics_metrics.description: Like \pgfpointborderrectangle but for an ellipse: returns the intersection of a ray from origin toward (direction point) and an ellipse whose bounding rectangle corner is (corner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same normalization remarks as for rectangles; examples show usage with an ellipse drawn via \pgfpathellipse.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfpointintersectionoflines
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the intersection of the line through p and q and the line through s and t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the lines do not intersect, an arithmetic overflow will occur (warning). Example demonstrates computing intersection of two drawn lines and placing a small circle at that point.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfextractx / \pgfextracty
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfextractx{<dimension>}{<point>} sets the TeX <dimension> to the x-coordinate of <point>. \pgfextracty similarly for the y-coordinate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \newdimen\mydim; \pgfextractx{\mydim}{\pgfpoint{2cm}{4pt}} yields \mydim = 2cm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internals: how point commands work (\pgf@x, \pgf@y, \pgf@process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Point commands set the TEX-dimensions \pgf@x and \pgf@y to the x and y components respectively; path-using commands just execute the coordinate parameter and then read \pgf@x and \pgf@y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because some point commands modify other variables, wrap point evaluation in a TeX scope and make \pgf@x and \pgf@y global, or use \pgf@process{<code>} which executes <code> in a scope and then makes \pgf@x and \pgf@y global. Do not keep important data in \pgf@x/\pgf@y (they are overwritten often); use \pgf@xa, \pgf@xb, \pgf@xc and \pgf@ya, \pgf@yb, \pgf@yc for intermediates. Example: definition of \pgfpointadd shows recommended pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Path concept and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: A path is the basic drawing entity and consists of parts (open or closed curves), where open curves have start and end points and segments can be straight or Bézier curves. A path by itself has no effect until used (stroking/drawing or filling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filling requires closed parts; the current path persists across TeX groups and is flushed when \pgfusepath is called. Path ops update bounding boxes (current path and picture).

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfpathmoveto (Move-To)
rubrics_metrics.description: Starts a path (or starts a new part when the current path is non-empty) at the specified coordinate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically must be given at beginning of a path (some commands generate implicit move-tos). Applies the current coordinate transformation matrix (CTM) to the coordinate and updates bounding boxes. If used to start a new part, it ends the previous part.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfpathlineto (Line-To)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extends the current path in a straight line to the given coordinate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should not be the first path construction command (a missing initial move-to may compile but render errors can occur). Applies CTM and updates bounding boxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfpathcurveto (Curve-To)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extends the current path with a Bézier curve from the last point to the specified coordinate, using two support points (support1, support2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May not be the first path operation. The bounding box is enlarged to encompass the two support points and endpoint, which guarantees containment but can make the bounding box overly large; tightening this would require non-trivial math.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfpathclose (Close Path)
rubrics_metrics.description: Closes the current part of the path by appending a straight line from the current point to the start point of that part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a difference between closing a part and adding a straight line to the start point using line-to; examples demonstrate differences in corner geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfpatharc (Arc path)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appends an arc (part of a circle or ellipse) between start angle and end angle on a circle of given radius (optional y-radius for an ellipse), moved so that its start point is the current last point of the path.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If start_angle < end_angle the curve goes counterclockwise. The command does not start a new part of the path (important for fill behavior). Using \pgfpatharc{0}{360}{1cm} 'nearly' gives a full circle; use \pgfpathclose to close. CTM affects arc; unless rotation/shearing applied, bounding box is tight. Use optional y-radius to form ellipses.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfpatharcaxes
rubrics_metrics.description: Like \pgfpatharc but specifies the ellipse by its 0°-axis and 90°-axis vectors instead of x- and y-radius.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example equivalence: \pgfpatharc{0}{90}{1cm/2cm} equals \pgfpatharcaxes{0}{90}{\pgfpoint{1cm}{0cm}}{\pgfpoint{0cm}{2cm}}. Applies CTM and updates bounding boxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfpathellipse / \pgfpathcircle
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfpathellipse appends a conceptual ellipse given center and two axis vectors (starts a new part if path not empty). \pgfpathcircle is a shorthand producing an axis-aligned circle (using pathellipse with axis vectors (radius,0) and (0,radius)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CTM is applied only after the ellipse is 'finished conceptually' (e.g., a translation shifts center rather than modifying axis vectors). Bounding boxes updated; this is faster and easier than constructing with move/arc/close sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfpathrectangle / \pgfpathrectanglecorners
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfpathrectangle{<corner>}{<diagonal vector>} adds a rectangle with one corner and diagonal vector. \pgfpathrectanglecorners{<corner>}{<opposite corner>} adds a rectangle by two opposing corners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both start a new part of the path, apply CTM, and update bounding boxes tightly. Examples show multiple rectangles drawn and stroked.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfpathgrid
rubrics_metrics.description: Appends a grid (many horizontal/vertical line segments) to the current path clipped conceptually to the rectangle between lower-left and upper-right points (but no actual clipping performed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: stepx=⟨dim⟩ (default 1cm), stepy=⟨dim⟩, or step=⟨vector⟩ to set both. Origin is considered part of the grid. The command computes entry/exit points and adds simple line segments. CTM is applied after the grid is conceptually finished; bounding boxes are updated tightly.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfpathparabola
rubrics_metrics.description: Appends two half-parabolas to the current path: first from current point to current + bend vector (the bend point), then from bend point to bend + end vector. If end vector is zero, only first half; if bend vector is zero, only second half.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cannot produce a parabola part that does not contain the bend. CTM is applied and bounding boxes updated. Examples show half-parabola, full parabola, and direction variations.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfpathsine / \pgfpathcosine
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfpathsine{<vector>} appends a sine curve over [0, π/2] starting at current point and ending at current+vector. \pgfpathcosine does the analogous cosine curve over [0, π/2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The curve is squeezed or stretched to the endpoint vector; chaining multiple sine/cosine ops can produce a full sine/cosine wave. CTM applied and bounding boxes updated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot path operations (pgfbaseplot)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are commands (documented in Section 56) for appending plots to a path via the pgfbaseplot package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section notes their existence but refers to Section 56 for details (placeholder/forward reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfsetcornersarced (Rounded corners)
rubrics_metrics.description: Causes subsequent corners to be replaced by little arcs; the effect lasts until the end of the current TeX scope. The provided point dictates how large the corner arc is: x-dim shortens the entering line, y-dim shortens the leaving line, then connect shortened lines by an arc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If x and y coordinates are equal and the corner is right angle you get a near-perfect quarter circle (approx up to six decimals). Rounding affects nearly all corners, including those from \pgfpathclose. To return to normal use \pgfsetcornersarced{\pgfpointorigin}. Warning: rounding produces undesirable effects if lines at corners are too short (shortening may cause lines to extend past other ends).

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal tracking of bounding boxes (path & picture variables)
rubrics_metrics.description: The system tracks two bounding boxes via dimension variables: current path bounding box (\pgf@pathminx, \pgf@pathmaxx, \pgf@pathminy, \pgf@pathmaxy) and current picture bounding box (\pgf@picminx, \pgf@picmaxx, \pgf@picminy, \pgf@picmaxy). Initial extreme values are set to ±16000pt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each path construction command globally updates these variables. Use \pgf@protocolsizes{<x-dim>}{<y-dim>} to update both bounding boxes to include the specified point. For picture bounding box updates, the update only occurs if the conditional \ifpgf@relevantforpicturesize is true.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgf@relevantforpicturesizefalse / \pgf@relevantforpicturesizetrue
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX if-switch to locally decide whether path construction commands should update the picture's bounding box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clipping commands set this if to false (and certain other commands do likewise) to avoid parts outside clipping area affecting the picture bounding box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Snakes: overview
rubrics_metrics.description: A snake is a way of adding a winding line to a path; snakes are made up of repeated little segments and they 'follow along' a straight line to a target point (rotated appropriately when target is not to the right).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Snakes can contain move-to operations and split paths into many subpaths. Snakes must be declared (describing segments and ordering) before use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaring snake segments
rubrics_metrics.description: When declaring a snake, each segment's rendering should be described as if the target lay at (+∞,0) and the segment's start at the origin; the pgf system will apply appropriate coordinate transforms when appending segments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not issue a \pgfpathmoveto{\pgfpointorigin} at the beginning of a segment (that would create many subpaths). You must provide segment widths and stopping information manually (pgf does not compute them automatically).

rubrics_metrics.name: Snake automata (finite automaton design)
rubrics_metrics.description: Snakes may have multiple segments and use finite-automaton style states to decide which segment to use where. Each state has rules of the form 'if the remaining distance is less than x, switch to state q' and a width parameter; processing checks switch rules first, then executes the state's code, translates by the width, reduces remaining distance, and possibly switches state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processing stops when the final state is reached (final state's segment is added immediately). The automaton mechanism enables special start/end segments and complex behavior like growing/shrinking segments in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfdeclaresnake
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfdeclaresnake{<name>}{<initial state>}{<states>} declares a new snake with the given initial state and a description of states (each state declared via \state commands inside the <states> argument).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The \state macro is defined only when the <states> argument is executed. Example demonstrates a simple 'example snake' declaration and using \draw[snake=example snake] ... to create snakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: \state command and options in snakes
rubrics_metrics.description: \state{<name>}[<options>]{<code>} declares a state; when in the state: (1) options parsed (may cause immediate state switch), (2) code executed (coordinate transform set so origin at start, target east), (3) after code, state switches to 'next state' if specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed options: switch if less than=<dimension> to <new state> (immediate switch if remaining distance < dim); width=<dimension> (tells pgf the width to translate the coordinate system by after adding the segment; also causes immediate switch to 'final' if remaining distance < width); next state=<state>. Two dimensions available: \pgfsnakeremainingdistance and \pgfsnakecompleteddistance hold remaining and completed distances respectively. Examples show more complex behavior using these variables and conditional logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predefined snakes and extensibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Only two very simple snakes are predefined when pgf is loaded: 'Snake lineto' (a straight line) and 'Snake moveto'. More interesting snakes are provided by the pgflibrarysnakes package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These trivial snakes are mainly useful as subsnakes or building blocks for more complex snake declarations in libraries.
